newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: TA sees limited upside for KL stocks.
newsitem.headline: TA sees limited upside for KL stocks.

text.p: A leading Malaysian stockbroker said on Tuesday the stock market has stabilised but the key market index's upside will not be far from the current 1,000-point level by the year's end.

"We believe that the market has stabilised. The currency problems...I think all these have abated," said Tony Tiah, executive chairman and managing director of stockbroking and financial services firm TA Enterprise Bhd.
The key Kuala Lumpur Composite Index "should fluctuate around the 1,000 range, 1,100", Tiah told reporters after TA's annual meeting, when asked where he sees the index by the end of the year.
The Composite Index ended midday trading on Tuesday at 1,030.87 points, down 19.4 percent from its 1997 high of 1,278.94 points.
The market has this year been hit by property and share-buying curbs introduced by the government, volatility in regional currencies and rising interest rates.
Tiah said market performance should improve in the next six to 12 months.
Asked whether recent low share-trading volumes is a worry for stockbroking firms, he said: "You can't pick one or two months. You have to average out over a period of six months to one year."

Tiah said said foreign funds, which have been blamed for the domestic financial markets' recent downturn, would return once conditions have improved. "They will only come back when they smell profit."
